message.content: The t12 probe revealed the actual bug in my pattern generation: sign-bit inputs shift to `i>>10 == 0x3F` (0x1F | sign), so my NaN/Inf exclusion missed negative non-finites. Fixing the mask to `(i>>10)&0x1F != 0x1F` and re-running the exhaustive sweep for c1.

function.arguments:
{"claim_id": "c1", "code": "import sys, json
sys.path.insert(0, "/root/cases/case_149")
import numpy as np, torch, kernel

# all finite FP16 bit patterns (exclude NaN/Inf: exponent field 0x1F, with sign-bit-aware mask)
bits = np.array([i for i in range(65536) if ((i >> 10) & 0x1F) != 0x1F], dtype=np.uint16)
x_np = np.frombuffer(bits.tobytes(), dtype=np.float16).copy()
x = torch.from_numpy(x_np).to("cuda")
assert torch.isfinite(x).all(), "nonfinite leaked"
assert x.numel() <= 131072

out = kernel.run(x)
ref = kernel.reference(x)
ok = out.view(torch.int16) == ref.view(torch.int16)
mismatches = (~ok).nonzero().flatten()
n_mismatch = int(mismatches.numel())
fail = []
for idx in mismatches[:12].tolist():
    fail.append({"x": x[idx].item(),
                 "x_bits": hex(int(bits[idx])),
                 "got_bits": hex(int(out[idx].view(torch.int16).item()) & 0xFFFF),
                 "got": out[idx].item(),
                 "want_bits": hex(int(ref[idx].view(torch.int16).item()) & 0xFFFF),
                 "want": ref[idx].item()})
print(json.dumps({"n_tested": int(x.numel()), "n_mismatch": n_mismatch,
                  "first_failures": fail}))
", "expected_signal": "count of bit-exact mismatches vs reference over all 64512 finite FP16 inputs"}

message.reasoning_content: The last probe (t12) still included NaNs — my exclusion `(i >> 10) != 0x1F` should have excluded 0xfc00 (exponent 0x1F). Wait 0xfc00 >> 10 = 0x1F... 0xfc00 = 1111110000000000, exponent bits 11111 → 0x1F, sign 1. i >> 10 with sign bit set: 0xfc00 >> 10 = 0x3F, not 0x1F! Because Python ints are fine, 0xfc00>>10 = 63. So need ((i >> 10) & 0x1F) != 0x1F. That's the bug. Run c1 again with fixed mask.
